ap_precalculus-f01.title: Dock water depth modeled by a sinusoidal function

stimulus.description: The depth of water at a dock, in feet, at time $t$ hours after midnight is modeled by $D(t)=12+3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}t\right)$ for $0\le t\le 12$. A graphing calculator is required for these questions.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of $D$ over the interval $1\le t\le 4$. Using correct units, interpret the meaning of your answer in the context of the problem.

rubric_rows.criterion: Average rate of change value
Interpretation with units: average change in depth per hour over the interval

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Find the first time $t>0$ at which the depth is $13.2$ feet.

rubric_rows.criterion: Equation setting the model equal to the depth
Solution value of the first time

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: For how many hours during $0\le t\le 12$ is the depth greater than $13.5$ feet?
parts.model_answer: The depth crosses $13.5$ feet at $t\approx1.000$ and $t\approx5.000$, so the duration is about 4.000 hours.

rubric_rows.criterion: Duration value with units

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: What is the period of $D$, and what does it mean in the context of the problem?
parts.model_answer: The period is 12 hours: the depth pattern repeats every 12 hours.

rubric_rows.criterion: States the period of 12 hours and that the depth pattern repeats every 12 hours

ap_precalculus-f02.title: Tea temperature modeled by a shifted exponential function

stimulus.description: The temperature of a cup of tea, in degrees Celsius, $t$ minutes after it is poured is modeled by $T(t)=80\cdot (0.82)^t+20$ for $t\ge 0$. A graphing calculator is required for these questions.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Find $T(3)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of the function with units

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of $T$ over the interval $2\le t\le 8$, and use its sign to describe how the temperature changes on the interval.
parts.model_answer: $\dfrac{T(8)-T(2)}{6}\approx-6.240$ degrees per minute; the negative value means the temperature decreases on average.

rubric_rows.criterion: Average rate of change value
Uses the sign to state that the temperature is decreasing on average

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: At what time $t$ is the temperature of the tea $32$ degrees Celsius?

rubric_rows.criterion: Equation setting the model equal to the temperature
Solution value of the time

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: As $t$ increases without bound, what value does $T(t)$ approach, and what does it mean in the context of the problem?
parts.model_answer: $T(t)$ approaches 20 degrees Celsius, the temperature of the room that the tea cools toward.

rubric_rows.criterion: States the value 20 and interprets it as the temperature the tea approaches
